newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian government to move in bitter pay dispute.
newsitem.headline: Italian government to move in bitter pay dispute.

text.p: Italian Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said on Saturday he would meet trades unions and industry leaders next week in an effort to settle a bitter pay dispute.

Unions representing some 1.5 million engineering and metalworkers recently held two eight-hour strikes and have threatened further stoppages if the employers' association, Federmeccanica, does not meet their pay demands.
Treu said he had called a meeting with the two sides next Thursday to try and solve the sticky issue.
"It will be a difficult mediation but the government wants an active, positive and useful role," Treu told a conference on unemployment in the northern city of Verona.
Prime Minister Romano Proid's centre-left government had said it would seek a solution if Federmeccanica did not return to the bargaining table by November 28.

On Monday, the three unions called for a further six hours of strikes to press their demands for management to compensate workers in full for higher-than-expected inflation in the past contractual period.
A four-hour stoppage had already been scheduled for December 13, when other sectors are expected to halt work in the metalworkers' support.

In cash terms, unions want a gross 262,000 lire ($173) rise in their monthly pay packets, of which 97,000 is to cover the overrun in inflation between 1994 and 1996. Employers have offered 195,000 lire of which just 30,000 is for inflation. ($1=1514 Lire)
